doc.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: His first Metronome All-Stars session in 1946
summary: He replaced Benny Goodman on the first All-Stars date alongside Parker and Gillespie.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Well, I mean, in talking about some of this, it’s probably noteworthy to say in ’46 you got your first Metronome All-Stars session, is that right?
Right. Murphy:…I mean, it was Charlie Parker…
Charlie Ventura, Charlie Parker. Was Lennie Tristano?
So that first one in ‘46, you actually were replacing Benny Goodman, isn’t that right?
Wow. How did you find that out?
I read the books. DeFranco. Ah, ‘cause I couldn’t remember. But it’s very possible, yeah, that Benny was considered number and I, he couldn’t make it and I replaced him. Yeah, that sounds familiar.
That must have been a lot of pressure. [laughter]
Yeah, but I was kind of used to pressure I guess, you can guess by that time.
